cands.name: Ocean Fitts
cands.bio: 27-year-old 'seventh-generation Floridian' studying Public Policy at St. Petersburg College; the only Democrat to qualify for the HD 71 ballot.
cands.local_ties: Described as a seventh-generation Floridian; city/county of residence not found in sources checked (an earlier search summary calling him 'Palmetto-based' appears to have confused him with a different Palmetto candidate, so it is not asserted).

record.text: No public office held. Platform: restore home rule, protect wetlands and environmental resources, invest in infrastructure and in public schools that are not politicized.

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: The Bradenton Times editorial board recommended Fitts for HD 71.

local_issue_stance.text: Advocates restoring home rule (reversing state preemption of local governments) and protecting wetlands.

cands.name: Jordan Varnadore
cands.race: Florida House District 71 (open seat; Will Robinson leaving, term-limited)
cands.bio: Vice President of Marketing at GarrettRichard, a Palmetto-based commercial insurance and PEO brokerage co-founded with his father; University of Mississippi (marketing/communications 2011); performs locally as a dueling pianist. Won the Aug 18, 2026 Republican primary with about 62% over Melton Little and Dylan Modarelli.
cands.local_ties: Lifelong Manatee County resident, Palmetto High School class of 2006, Palmetto-based business; Florida GOP leadership appointed him Secretary of the Manatee County Republican Executive Committee after the state party disbanded the locally elected committee.

record.text: No legislative record. Self-described 'proud America-First conservative'; platform: reduce burdensome regulations, parental say in schools and 'values not extremist ideologies', Second Amendment.
Appointed Secretary of the Manatee County Republican Executive Committee by Florida GOP leadership after the state party suspended the local committee following the 2024 primary.
Campaign records show payments to Three Seas Consulting LLC (Nicholas Catroppo).

money_notes.text: As of the latest pre-primary report: $76,995 in monetary and $990 in-kind contributions; ~$28,746 spent. Mostly Manatee-based donors; at least $7,000 from businesses/individuals tied to Conley Buick GMC.

Maximum contributions from Parents First PC (chaired by Manatee School Board member Chad Choate) and five committees chaired by Thomas Piccolo of Tampa firm SIMWINS: Unifying Leadership for Florida, Protecting Florida's Progress, Conservative for Florida, United for Florida, Conservatives Standing Proudly for Common Sense.

Also gave: Associated Industries of Florida PAC, Conservatives for Florida Agriculture PAC, and Floridians United for a Sustainable Economy PC (chaired by Jon Mast, CEO of the Suncoast Builders Association).

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: No endorsements listed on BallotReady or in the Bradenton Times primary profile; (reported max-donor committees listed under money_notes).

local_issue_stance.text: No explicit stance on wetlands, SB 180 or HB 399 found; campaign emphasizes reducing regulation on job creators. Bradenton Times editorial expects pro-preemption votes (opinion).
